Executive Order 11036
ADMINISTRATION OF THE AGRICULTURAL TRADE DEVELOPMENT AND  
ASSISTANCE ACT OF 1954, AS AMENDED
B y virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
o f the United States Code, and as President o f the United States, it 
is ordered that Executive Order No. 10900 of January 5, 1961, as 
amended, be, and it is hereby, further amended as follow s:
( I )  B y substituting for Section 4 (a ) the following:
“ S e c. 4. Foreign currencies,  (a )(1 ) Foreign currencies which ac­
crue under Title I  of the Act may be used for the purposes set forth 
in Section 104 of the A ct in amounts consonant with applicable pro­
visions o f law and of sales agreements and loan agreements. E x­
cept as may be inconsistent with such law or agreements, priority 
shall be accorded to the sale of such currencies to appropriations 
or to their sale otherwise for dollars. To such extent as he may deem 
necessary, the Director o f the Bureau of the Budget shall fix the 
amounts of such currencies to be Used for the purposes set forth in

Section 104. The Director shall notify the Secretary of the Treasury 
with respect to any amounts so fixed.
“ (2) The function conferred upon the'President by the penultimate 
proviso o f Section 104 o f the A ct of waiving the applicability of 
Section 1415 o f the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1953 (31 U.S.C. 
724), is hereby delegated to the Secretary o f State in respect of Section 
104(e) o f the Act and to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget 
in all other respects.”
( I I )  B y inserting the following new paragraph after Section 4 (d )
“ (5) Those under Section 104(s) of the A ct by the Department o f 
the Treasury in consultation with the Department of State. The 
function conferred upon the President by Section 104 (s) o f the Act 
o f prescribing terms and conditions is hereby delegated to‘ the Secre­
tary o f the Treasury and shall be performed by him in consultation 
with the Secretary o f State.”
( I l l )  B y substituting for Section 4 (d ) (7) the following:
“ (7) Those under Section 104(g) o f the Act by the Department of 
State. The function conferred upon the President by Section 104(g) 
o f the A ct of determining the manner in which the loans provided for 
in that section shall be made is hereby delegated to the Secretary of 
State.”

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 6653) prints Executive Order 11036 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-07-11; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954, as amended). I read the whole text and signature block. Inventory: the dossier splits the order into two contiguous clauses at an OCR break inside amended Section 4(a)(1) (the second clause begins with a sentence fragment labelled Section 104). Together they cover amendments (I), (II) and (III) and the signature; I confirm the inventory as complete and decide both clauses as parts of one amending order. The order further amends Executive Order No. 10900 of January 5, 1961, as amended (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954): (I) it substitutes a new Section 4(a), under which the Director of the Bureau of the Budget fixes the amounts of foreign currencies accruing under Title I to be used for section 104 purposes and notifies the Secretary of the Treasury, and the waiver function of the penultimate proviso of section 104 is delegated to the Secretary of State for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget otherwise; (II) it inserts a new paragraph (5) in Section 4(d) assigning section 104(s) purposes to the Department of the Treasury in consultation with the Department of State and delegating the terms-and-conditions function to the Secretary of the Treasury; and (III) it substitutes a new Section 4(d)(7) assigning section 104(g) purposes to the Department of State and delegating the loan-manner function to the Secretary of State. Ending: Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980 (45 FR 44245, Federal Register of July 1, 1980; the complete held Federal Register text) provides in section 1-501 that Executive Order No. 10900 of January 5, 1961, as amended, is revoked. Because this order's text is part of Executive Order 10900 as amended, that revocation reaches it, and the same order re-delegates each function in revised form: section 1-401(a) addresses the use of foreign currencies, the fixing of amounts by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the notice to the Treasury, section 1-401(b) re-delegates the waiver function (to the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget otherwise), section 1-405(a) re-delegates the loan-manner function formerly in Section 4(d)(7), and section 1-405(b) re-delegates the terms-and-conditions function formerly in Section 4(d)(5) to the Secretary of the Treasury in consultation with the Secretary of State. The held text has no effective-date wording and is headed as an order of June 27, 1980, so I read 1980-06-27 as the effective date; the alternative reading is the publication date, 1980-07-01. The dossier's located-provision record for this pair uses a transcription mirror of EO 12220; I did not rely on it and cite the Federal Register text instead. Savings: the functions continue under Executive Order 12220, which re-delegates them in revised form; EO 12220 has no express savings clause in the held text (reviewed in full). Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The own text sets no end. I checked each intervening instrument in the dossier. Executive Order 11252 (1965-10-20) transfers the functions of the Director of the Food-For-Peace Program to the Secretary of State and modifies Executive Order 10900 accordingly; the functions delegated here run to the Budget Director, the Treasury and State, not that Director. Executive Order 11963 (1977-01-19) adds a subsection to Section 1 of Executive Order 10900. Executive Order 12148 (1979-07-20), in section 5-108, revokes only Section 4(d)(2) of Executive Order 10900, a paragraph this order does not touch. Executive Order 12163 (1979-09-29) amends Section 3 of Executive Order 10900 and revokes other orders. None of these ends these clauses; amendments are later events, not ends. The held text of Executive Order 11836, which the dossier lists as citing this order by number, prints the number 11036 over a different subject (the Transportation Cargo Security Program) and refers to neither Executive Order 10900 nor the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act, so it is not an event for this order. The first ending shown by held evidence is section 1-501 of Executive Order 12220, effective 1980-06-27.","independent_command_check":"Each clause only amends Executive Order 10900; none is a command independent of that order. The parent order was revoked as a whole by section 1-501 of Executive Order 12220, so no surviving parent text carries these amendments.","savings_check":"The substance of each delegation continued, in revised form, under sections 1-401 and 1-405 of Executive Order 12220, which also revoked the parent; no continuing command of this order outside that restatement was found, and no express savings clause appears in the held text of Executive Order 12220.","scope_check":"Two clauses cover the whole order; amendments (I), (II) and (III) are all part of Executive Order 10900 as amended and ended together when Executive Order 12220 revoked that order as amended."}

savings_residuals.reason: The delegations amended or added by this order were re-delegated in revised form in sections 1-401(a)-(b) and 1-405(a)-(b) of Executive Order 12220, which revoked Executive Order 10900 as amended on 1980-06-27; the functions therefore continued, with revised delegates in places, under the new order. The held text of Executive Order 12220 has no express savings clause, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or Federal Register catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.
